question: What is the primary target population for standard precautions in a healthcare facility?

options.A: Only patients with confirmed viral infections
options.B: Surgical patients admitted for elective procedures

explanation: Standard precautions are designed to be applied universally to every patient care encounter, maintaining safety regardless of infection status. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h1)

question: Why must standard precautions be applied even when a patient has no known infectious disease?

options.A: Hospital accreditation standards mandate full PPE for routine bedmaking
options.B: Asymptomatic individuals can still harbor and transmit pathogenic agents
options.C: Pathogens only survive on surfaces when a patient shows active symptoms
options.D: Detergents used in cleaning are too harsh for unprotected hands

explanation: Many patients carry infectious agents without showing overt symptoms, making universal baseline precautions necessary to prevent silent transmission. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h1)

question: Which PPE items are routinely required when entering the room of a patient placed on contact precautions?

options.B: Head cap and heavy utility gloves

explanation: Contact precautions primarily require gowns and gloves to prevent skin-to-skin contact and contamination of clothing from infectious surfaces. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h2)

question: A nurse is caring for a patient admitted with a draining wound infected with a methicillin-resistant organism. Which action best prevents indirect contact transmission?

options.A: Performing hand hygiene and changing gloves between handling the wound and touching clean environmental surfaces
options.B: Applying a standard surgical mask before entering the patient's personal zone
options.C: Keeping the patient's room door tightly closed at all times while maintaining negative pressure
options.D: Restricting all family visits until systemic antibiotic therapy is completed

explanation: Indirect contact often happens when contaminated hands or gloves transfer pathogens from a dirty site to clean equipment or surfaces within the room. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h2)

question: What is the maximum approximate distance that large respiratory droplets typically travel through the air before settling?
explanation: Large droplets are relatively heavy and fall quickly, rarely traveling beyond one to two meters from the source. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h3)

question: Which condition is a classic indication for initiating droplet precautions?
explanation: Influenza is primarily spread via large respiratory droplets during close contact, requiring droplet barriers. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h3)

question: Which piece of respiratory protection is required for healthcare workers entering an airborne infection isolation room?
explanation: Airborne precautions demand specialized particulate respirators capable of filtering out microscopic droplet nuclei. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h4)

question: What is the primary function of negative pressure ventilation in an airborne isolation room?

options.A: Increasing ambient room temperature to destroy heat-sensitive viral particles
options.B: Preventing contaminated room air from escaping into public hallways when the door is opened
options.C: Accelerating the chemical evaporation of surface disinfectants applied to floors
options.D: Reducing humidity levels to prevent fungal spore germination within the ventilation ducts

explanation: Negative pressure ensures that airflow moves inward from clean corridors into the isolation room, trapping infectious aerosols inside. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h4)

question: Which item of personal protective equipment is typically removed first during the doffing sequence?
explanation: Gloves are removed first because they are the most heavily contaminated item and pose an immediate touch hazard to other surfaces. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h5)

question: Why is the sequence of donning and doffing personal protective equipment strictly standardized in clinical training?

options.A: To comply with aesthetic guidelines established for hospital branding
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing disposable medical supplies
options.C: To minimize the risk of self-contamination during application and removal
options.D: To accelerate the speed of emergency response during cardiac arrests

explanation: Standardized sequencing ensures that clean areas are not touched by contaminated surfaces during the hazardous removal phase. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h5)

question: What is an essential preliminary step before transporting a patient on airborne precautions to another department?

options.A: Removing all intravenous lines and monitoring equipment
options.B: Administering a prophylactic dose of antibiotics
options.D: Notifying the receiving department in advance

explanation: Advance notification allows the receiving unit to prepare for the patient's arrival and prevent unnecessary exposure of other patients in waiting areas. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h6)

question: Which items in a patient's room require the most frequent cleaning and disinfection attention?

options.B: High-touch surfaces like bedrails and call buttons
options.C: Ceiling tiles and upper window glass panes
options.D: Interior walls behind large stationary wardrobes

explanation: High-touch surfaces are repeatedly contaminated by hands, serving as primary vehicles for indirect contact transmission. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h6)

question: How do nurses in resource-constrained Nigerian settings often adapt when mechanical ventilation for airborne isolation fails due to power outages?

options.A: Transferring every infectious patient immediately to private outdoor tents
options.B: Utilizing natural cross-ventilation through open architectural windows and strategic ward placement
options.C: Requiring all visitors to wear heavy rubber aprons in place of physical barriers
options.D: Suspending all patient admissions until electrical grid repairs are fully completed

explanation: When mechanical systems fail, maximizing natural airflow through architectural design helps disperse airborne droplet nuclei in resource-limited environments. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h7)

question: Which factor most frequently complicates the routine implementation of transmission-based precautions in busy public hospitals?

options.A: Shortages of disposable personal protective equipment
options.B: Over-abundance of trained infectious disease specialists
options.C: Strict patient compliance with single-room isolation
options.D: An excess of negative pressure isolation rooms

explanation: Resource limitations often result in supply chain constraints regarding single-use PPE, requiring careful rationing and alternative control strategies. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h7)
